coverage_note: Read all 1159 turns. Gaps at 06:16-06:34 (Amal stepped away) and 42:53-44:34 / 45:51-46:53 (Medi stepped away). Several engine mishearings: 03:46 فمي for تمي (mouth) which Medi self-fixed to بطني at 03:50; 04:20 نانا for نعنع; 06:16/06:34 تشرب ليون for شو اليوم; 06:59 جدSA for قديش الساعة; 09:44 قارة for أرض; 14:03 elbowss are then for البوظة إذاً; 51:54 ٱش ٱش for حشيش; 1:10:34 مع الشوق بك for بشوفك. Latin-transliterated stretches in Medi's speech around 38:06-40:00 and 54:26.

rows.medi_said: Uh, عشان خطيبتي.
rows.why: عشان is followed by a clause or verb (or من/بسبب for 'because of my fiancée'), though colloquial shorthand is possible; Amal let it pass.

rows.medi_said: كنت أحسن؟
rows.why: Medi asked how to say the idiom 'I've been better' by testing كنت أحسن and صرت, and Amal explained Arabic doesn't have present perfect for this.

rows.medi_said: بس خطيبتي، um, أحسن،
rows.why: Medi omitted the verb صارت ('became/got better') and Amal recast it as صارت أحسن؟ which Medi accepted ('Oh. Became better, yeah').

rows.medi_said: أنا راح أطلب، uh, إلها is it أط-- أطلب لها؟
rows.amal_said: You're gonna ask of her? You-- or you're gonna order for her? ... So.
rows.why: أطلب takes من when asking/requesting something from someone (بطلب من), not لـ; Amal prompted in English until he fixed it to أطلب منها.
rows.english: I am going to ask her (request from her).

rows.medi_said: ف-أ-أطلب منها، uh um, هي تشتري، uh, نعنع
rows.why: After أطلب منها the subjunctive verb تشتري follows directly without repeating the subject pronoun هي; Amal let the pronoun pass.
rows.english: I'll ask her to buy mint.

rows.medi_said: اليوم جمعة،
rows.why: Days of the week take el- (اليوم الجمعة / يوم الجمعة); Amal let it pass.

rows.medi_said: ثنتين إلا عشرة، عـ- عشرة، عشـ-- عشر-- دقايق دقائق.
rows.why: Before a plural counted noun, 10 takes the short form عشر (عشر دقايق); Medi hesitated between عشرة and عشر-- and Amal let it pass.

rows.medi_said: Hold on. Less was it um, ألأ؟ شوي-- شوي ألأ شوب.
rows.why: Medi could not recall the form of أقل ('less') and said ألأ; Amal asked إيش يعني؟ and supplied أقل.

rows.medi_said: طبيعة. الكلمة الطبيعة.
rows.why: Amal asked for plural 'words' (كلمات) and in idafa ('nature words') the first noun takes no el- (كلمات الطبيعة, not الكلمة الطبيعة).

rows.medi_said: الكلمات الطبيعات.
rows.amal_said: كلمات الطبيعة. ... لا، طبيعة just nature.
rows.why: Medi kept el- on the first noun of idafa (A2) and pluralized the uncountable noun طبيعة to الطبيعات (A9); Amal recast to كلمات الطبيعة.

rows.medi_said: قمر؟ قمر؟
rows.why: Amal asked for hidden-gender feminine nouns that sound masculine (A18) and Medi guessed قمر (which is masculine); Amal said No.

rows.medi_said: نسيت.
rows.why: Amal asked for the word that sounds feminine but is masculine (A18); Medi said نسيت ('I forgot') and Amal supplied هوا.

rows.medi_said: المفضل؟ ... إشي؟ ... هو؟
rows.amal_said: شو كمان؟ شو بزيد؟ ... No. ... المفضل عندي.
rows.why: To say 'my favorite' on its own, المفضل needs عندي after it (A23); Medi guessed إشي and هو before Amal supplied المفضل عندي.

rows.medi_said: بوظة حلوة المفضل عنـ عندي
rows.why: As the subject of the sentence ('Sweet ice cream is my favorite'), both the noun and its adjective need el- (البوظة الحلوة).
rows.english: Sweet ice cream is my favorite.

rows.medi_said: So بوظة المفضل آآآ، عندي
rows.amal_said: Yeah ice cream. elbowss are then. [البوظة إذاً]
rows.why: When talking about ice cream in general as the subject ('Ice cream is my favorite'), it requires el- (البوظة); Amal corrected to البوظة (engine wrote 'elbowss are then').

rows.medi_said: So بوظة المفضل آآآ، عندي
rows.amal_said: Mm-hmm. ... I said it after you as well.
rows.why: بوظة is feminine, so مفضل must take the feminine ending المفضلة (A23/A8), which Amal typed in chat at 14:15 and confirmed at 15:39-16:27.

rows.medi_said: هدول الـ-- Is it مسلسلين؟
rows.why: After هدول ('these shows'), the plural of مسلسل is مسلسلات (feminine sound plural -aat), not مسلسلين.

rows.medi_said: مسلسلات. هدول المسلسلات، عندي المفضل... الـ مف-- آآآ، الـ مفضلين عندي؟
rows.why: Medi initially put عندي before المفضل and used singular, then self-corrected by asking الـ مفضلين عندي؟ which Amal confirmed.

rows.medi_said: So الـ مف-- الـ مف-- No. My favorite. Yeah. الـ مفضل. No. مفضل الـ. الـ مفضل الـ.
rows.why: Medi tried to put المفضل before the noun ('my favorite ice cream'), and Amal said 'No. No. No.' until he put the noun with possessive first (بوظتي المفضلة).

rows.medi_said: So جبالي.
rows.amal_said: No. This is my favorite. يعني my favorite's on its own, so we use the new one, the new way. ... جبال means my mountains.
rows.why: For 'Mountains are my favorite' (where 'my favorite' stands as predicate, not 'my mountains'), you use الجبال المفضلين عندي, not جبالي.

rows.medi_said: المفضل is-- جبال is masculine, right?
rows.why: Because الجبال is plural, the adjective مفضل must be pluralized to المفضلين (A23/A9).

rows.medi_said: جبال.
rows.why: Amal asked 'So one mountain is' and Medi said the plural جبال instead of the singular جبل.

rows.medi_said: One would be مبسوط؟
rows.amal_said: So it's, it's, uh, it's fun. It, it makes people happy.
rows.why: To say a lake is 'enjoyable / fun' (causes happiness), Arabic uses the causative verb بتبسط, not the participle مبسوط ('happy' for a person).
rows.english: The other lake is more enjoyable.

rows.medi_said: Um, the other lake. So بحيرة تاني.
rows.amal_said: The other lake. ... We corrected this fact.
rows.why: 'The other lake' (definite) requires el- on both noun and taani, plus feminine agreement on تانية: البحيرة التانية (A14/A21, A8).

rows.medi_said: So بحيرة التانية.
rows.why: Medi put el- on التانية but left it off بحيرة; Amal recast with el- on both: البحيرة الثانية.

rows.medi_said: بتبسطي. No، بتبس- ... بـ بتتـ بتتبسط.
rows.why: Medi first added the 'you (f)' -i ending (بتبسطي) and then an extra t- (بتتبسط) before settling on بتبسط for 'she/it (f) makes one happy'.

rows.medi_said: إذا ما بـ- بتحب هـ- هذه الـ شاطـ...
rows.chat: iza ma bet7ebbi hada el-sha66, e7na bne2dar nroo7 3ala sha66 taani
rows.why: شط is masculine, so it takes هذا, not هذه (A10).
rows.english: If you don't like this beach...

rows.medi_said: Uh, okay. إذا ما بـ- بتحب هـ-
rows.chat: iza ma bet7ebbi hada el-sha66, e7na bne2dar nroo7 3ala sha66 taani
rows.why: Speaking to Amal (female), 'you like' should be بتحبي (as she typed in chat: bet7ebbi), not masculine بتحب; she let it pass on voice.
rows.english: If you don't like this beach...

rows.medi_said: شو الكلمة لـ- لـ forest؟
rows.why: Medi asked 'شو الكلمة لـ forest؟' and Amal supplied غابة.

rows.medi_said: Okay. هذه الغابة uh, أول واحد...
rows.amal_said: غابة. ... Yes، بس غابة is what؟ ... It is so واحد أو واحدة.
rows.why: Referring back to the feminine noun غابة ('the first one'), 'one' must be feminine وحدة, not masculine واحد.
rows.english: This forest is the first one I go to.

rows.medi_said: So there's no الـ... Uh, no هذي الغابة. Okay. Ha-- uh, اللي...
rows.amal_said: No، you said أول غابة. So you don't need اللي. ... We're just saying أول واحدة is what we look at.
rows.why: أول وحدة is indefinite (no el-), so the relative clause follows directly without اللي (C7: no el-, no illi).
rows.english: This forest is the first one I go to.

rows.medi_said: أنا بر-- uh, I go to أنا بروح أو أنا بروحها. ... أنا بروحها?
rows.amal_said: أنا بروح to. ... بروح عليها. I go to.
rows.why: بروح takes the preposition على ('go to'), not a direct object suffix on the verb, so the pointer pronoun attaches to على: بروح عليها (D2/C2).

rows.medi_said: Does it have to do with "بختر" or no?
rows.amal_said: It has to do with مفضل.
rows.why: When asked if he remembered 'prefer', Medi asked if it was related to بختار and Amal prompted him with مفضل so he found بفضل.

rows.medi_said: Which view do you prefer? اه بتفضل منظر.
rows.why: Medi initially said masculine بتفضل at 30:18 before self-correcting to feminine بتفضلي at 30:35.

rows.medi_said: So، عادي نفس
rows.chat: hada nafs el-manzar illi shufto fi Madrid
rows.why: منظر is masculine, so 'this' must be هادا, not هادي (engine wrote عادي for Medi's هادي).
rows.english: This is the same view I saw in Madrid.

rows.medi_said: Is it منظرات؟ ... مناظير؟
rows.amal_said: No. It's the M group, do you remember? ... مناظر.
rows.why: The broken plural of منظر is مناظر (maCaaCeC pattern), not منظرات or مناظير.

rows.medi_said: I brought you. أنا جبت، جبتك.
rows.amal_said: I brought to you. ... mm، جبت لك.
rows.chat: ana jebtillek warda taanie 3ashan 3id milaadek el-yoam
rows.why: جبتك means 'I brought you (as the object)'; 'I brought for/to you' requires the preposition لـ: جبتلك (بجيب لـ).

rows.medi_said: هذا غير الـ...
rows.why: غير meaning 'a different/other' goes directly before an indefinite noun without el- (غير نوع).
rows.english: That is a different type of trees.

rows.medi_said: So هذا غير أنواع
rows.why: For singular 'that is a different type', use singular نوع, not the plural أنواع ('That's types').
rows.english: That is a different type of trees.

rows.medi_said: It, an-no' من, uh, sh-شجر.
rows.why: General collective nouns after من take el- (من الشجر, as Amal said at 40:19 and typed in chat), though Medi noticed it himself at 39:06 ('min il shajar').

rows.medi_said: Is it the same mukhtalif anwa? Mukhtalif nuwa?
rows.amal_said: لا، نوع مختلف. 'Cause مختلف is just an adjective. Can't be anything else.
rows.why: مختلف is a regular adjective, so it must come AFTER the noun (نوع مختلف), unlike غير.

rows.medi_said: من أول اليوم
rows.chat: min awal yoami, ana jarrabet anwaa3 mu5talefeen min el-akel
rows.why: Amal's prompt was 'Since the beginning of MY day' (من أول يومي), and Medi said 'the day' (أول اليوم) instead of using the possessive ending.
rows.english: Since the beginning of my day.

rows.medi_said: غير، أنواع من، uh, is just أكل؟ Is-- There's no plural for أكل، right؟ إلا أكل.
rows.chat: min awal yoami, ana jarrabet anwaa3 mu5talefeen min el-akel
rows.why: Talking about food in general after من ('types of food') requires the definite article el-: من الأكل.

rows.medi_said: أنا جربت أنواع أنواع مختلف الأكل. ... أنواع مختلفين الأكل.
rows.amal_said: مختلف من الأكل. ... من؟ Where's the من؟ ... من الأكل.
rows.chat: min awal yoami, ana jarrabet anwaa3 mu5talefeen min el-akel
rows.wrong: أنواع مختلف الأكل / أنواع مختلفين الأكل
rows.why: 'Different types of food' with an adjective on أنواع cannot be an idafa; it needs the preposition من before الأكل (أنواع مختلفين من الأكل / أنواع مختلفة من الأكل).
rows.english: I tried different types of food.

rows.medi_said: من أكل. Yeah، من أكل.
rows.chat: min awal yoami, ana jarrabet anwaa3 mu5talefeen min el-akel
rows.why: Medi dropped el- on الأكل again after من, and Amal recast to من الأكل.

rows.medi_said: أعطيني ثلاث، ثلاث ورقة، ثلاث ورقة.
rows.why: Numbers 3-10 take the countable plural form ورقات (تلات ورقات), not the singular ورقة (E1).

rows.medi_said: or أنا بحتاج uh, غير الـ ورقة.
rows.amal_said: ال never غير، غير never ends. [غير never takes الـ]
rows.why: غير meaning 'a different / another' takes an indefinite noun without el- (غير ورقة).

rows.medi_said: أنا بحتاج ورقة ورقة كمان.
rows.why: When كمان means 'another / one more', it must go BEFORE the noun: كمان ورقة (A19).

rows.medi_said: أغلب البيوت في أمريكي-- أمريكا عندهم.
rows.why: For inanimate places like houses having grass inside/at them, Arabic uses فيهم ('in them'), not عندهم (which is for people owning things).
rows.english: Most houses in America have grass.

rows.medi_said: Oh، فيهم. Is it حشاشيش؟ I forgot the plural.
rows.why: حشيش ('grass') is a collective/mass noun and does not take a plural here; Medi invented حشاشيش.
rows.english: Most houses in America have grass.

rows.medi_said: Um, I remember it was a Persian word. Hold on. ... Was it vazeh?
rows.why: Medi could not remember Arabic واضح ('clear') and said the Persian pronunciation vazeh; Amal supplied واضح.

rows.medi_said: آخر سؤالي ... سؤالي... wou- would it be سؤالي آـ... Would would it be سؤالي آخر إلي؟
rows.amal_said: No? It has two ways to say it. My question that is, mm, that is the last one, which is سؤالي الأخير. Or آخر سؤال إلي.
rows.why: آخر سؤالي means 'the end of my question'; to say 'my last question' you must use the adjective الأخير after the possessed noun (سؤالي الأخير) or آخر سؤال إلي (A15/A20).

rows.medi_said: هذا لعبي الأول.
rows.chat: haadi lu3beti el-oola / awal lu3be ili
rows.why: لعبة is a feminine noun ending in -e, so with 'my' it becomes لعبتي (growing -t, A3/A4) and takes feminine هادي (A10) and الأولى (A13/A8).

rows.medi_said: أول لعبة على على ثنتين، على
rows.amal_said: Mm-hmm. قلت انتين [التنتين]، بس very good.
rows.why: Clock time after على requires el- on the number when الساعة is omitted: على التنتين (A1/E2).
rows.english: The first game is at two.

rows.medi_said: لـ، uh, لعبة، لعبة تانية. لعبة تانية؟ ... لعبة تانية.
rows.why: لعبة تانية means 'another game'; for definite 'the other game', both words need el-: اللعبة التانية (A14/A21).
rows.english: The other game is more enjoyable.

rows.medi_said: Oh، آآآ أكتر أكتر آآآ أكتر، uh... آآآ بتبسط.
rows.why: أكتر ('more') goes AFTER the verb/adjective it modifies (بتبسط أكتر), not before it.
rows.english: The other game is more enjoyable.

rows.medi_said: آآآ أغلب الـ لُعب، آآآ لُعب، لُعبا-- لُعبات؟
rows.why: The plural of لعبة is the broken plural ألعاب, not لعبات.
rows.english: Most of the games here are cheap.

rows.medi_said: آخر لعبتي، no? ... آآآ لعبتي الـ آخر.
rows.amal_said: آخر لعبتي means the end of my games. ... اللعبة so feminine. Mm-hmm.
rows.chat: lu3beti el-a5eera / aa5er lu3be ili hoan el-yoam
rows.why: آخر لعبتي means 'the end of my game' (A20); 'my last game' uses the feminine adjective الأخيرة after the noun: لعبتي الأخيرة (A15/A8).
rows.english: My last game here is today.

rows.medi_said: آآآ آخر الـ لعبة. هادي آخر هادي آخر اللعبة إلي.
rows.amal_said: No, آخر اللعبة means end of.
rows.chat: lu3beti el-a5eera / aa5er lu3be ili hoan el-yoam
rows.why: آخر + el- + noun means 'the end of the game'; to mean 'last game' before إلي, the noun must be indefinite without el-: آخر لعبة إلي (A15/A20).

rows.medi_said: Yeah، آخر اللعبة، آآآ آآآ مـ... آآآ كـ... كانت بتزهق بتزهق.
rows.amal_said: كان and آخر. So كان بيزهى [بيزهق]. 'Cause I'm talking about آخر.
rows.why: In the idafa آخر اللعبة ('the end of the game'), the head noun is آخر (masculine), not اللعبة (feminine), so the verbs must be masculine كان بيزهق, not feminine كانت بتزهق (B18).
rows.english: The end of the game was boring.
